starshipEstimatedLaunch.summary: SpaceX’s launch page does not list an official Flight 14 date. As of September 14, Next Spaceflight lists the first orbital Starship attempt as no earlier than September 18, 2026; its listed time is an independent estimate, not an official SpaceX schedule.

stories.title: APOD: 2026 October 10 – Lunar Farside
stories.summary: The Moon's farside has a rough and battered surface that differs significantly from the nearside, which is covered with smooth, dark lunar maria. This difference is likely due to a thicker crust on the farside, which inhibits molten material from flowing to the surface to form maria.
stories.finding: The Moon's farside has a rough and battered surface that differs significantly from the nearside, which is covered with smooth, dark lunar maria. This difference is likely due to a thicker crust on the farside, which inhibits molten material from flowing to the surface to form maria.
stories.significance: Understanding the geological differences between the lunar nearside and farside provides insights into the Moon's formation and evolution, helping to explain its asymmetrical crustal thickness and surface features.
stories.caveat: The explanation for the difference in surface features between the nearside and farside is presented as a "likely explanation" rather than a confirmed fact, indicating it is a hypothesis based on observations.

stories.title: NASA Demonstrates Next-Generation Heat Shield Technologies
stories.summary: NASA is testing next-generation heat shield materials and designs, including 3D-printed heat shields and flexible MERINO materials, using experimental capsules carried aboard a Northrop Grumman Cygnus XL cargo spacecraft during its re-entry into Earth's atmosphere.

stories.significance: This method provides a cost-effective way to gather real-world flight data on new thermal protection systems, which are crucial for ensuring the safety of future crewed and uncrewed missions to destinations like the Moon and Mars.
stories.caveat: The source does not specify material limitations; independent verification is not established.

stories.title: Cosmic House of Mirrors
stories.summary: The James Webb Space Telescope captured an image of the galaxy cluster MACS J0454.1-0300, revealing distant galaxies whose light is bent and magnified by gravitational lensing, creating a "house of mirrors" effect.
stories.finding: The James Webb Space Telescope captured an image of the galaxy cluster MACS J0454.1-0300, revealing distant galaxies whose light is bent and magnified by gravitational lensing, creating a "house of mirrors" effect.
stories.significance: This phenomenon demonstrates how massive objects in space can distort and amplify light from more distant objects, providing insights into the distribution of mass and the nature of light in the universe.
stories.caveat: The source does not specify material limitations; independent verification is not established.

stories.title: APOD: 2026 October 9 – Stickney Crater
stories.summary: Streaks on Phobos suggest loose material slid down inside Stickney Crater walls over time, and light bluish regions near the crater's rim could indicate a relatively freshly exposed surface.
stories.finding: Streaks on Phobos suggest loose material slid down inside Stickney Crater walls over time, and light bluish regions near the crater's rim could indicate a relatively freshly exposed surface.
stories.significance: These observations provide clues about the geological processes occurring on Phobos, a moon of Mars, including potential recent surface activity and the nature of its composition.
stories.caveat: The source does not specify material limitations; independent verification is not established.

stories.title: Floodwaters Overwhelm Thailand
stories.summary: Persistent heavy rains in late September and early October 2026 caused widespread flooding across Thailand, inundating agricultural and aquaculture lands, particularly in Prachin Buri province along the Bang Pakong River.

stories.title: NASA Briefing to Highlight Contributions to Martian Moons Mission
stories.summary: NASA will contribute a gamma-ray and neutron spectrometer, a surface sampler mechanism, and communications and navigation support to Japan's Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission.
stories.finding: NASA will contribute a gamma-ray and neutron spectrometer, a surface sampler mechanism, and communications and navigation support to Japan's Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission.
stories.significance: These contributions will aid in the MMX mission's survey of Mars' moons, Phobos and Deimos, and the eventual collection and delivery of a surface sample from Phobos to Earth.
stories.caveat: The source does not specify material limitations; independent verification is not established.

stories.title: NASA’s SSPICY Mission to Demonstrate In-Space Inspection Technologies
stories.summary: The Small Spacecraft Propulsion and Inspection Capability (SSPICY) mission, launched on October 1, 2026, will demonstrate technologies for in-space inspection of defunct satellites and rocket bodies in low Earth orbit.
stories.finding: The Small Spacecraft Propulsion and Inspection Capability (SSPICY) mission, launched on October 1, 2026, will demonstrate technologies for in-space inspection of defunct satellites and rocket bodies in low Earth orbit.
stories.significance: This mission is crucial for developing future capabilities in autonomous servicing, orbital debris inspection, and potentially in-space repair or safe removal of space objects, which is increasingly critical for maintaining a safe operational environment in space.
stories.caveat: The mission is a technology demonstration and will not involve touching or docking with any satellites; it will only test the technologies needed for future servicing or repair missions. The results of these demonstrations are not yet available.

stories.title: Crew-12 Returns to Earth
stories.summary: The SpaceX Crew Dragon Freedom spacecraft, carrying NASA astronauts Jessica Meir and Jack Hathaway, ESA astronaut Sophie Adenot, and Roscosmos cosmonaut Andrey Fedyaev, successfully splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of California on October 8, 2026.
stories.finding: The SpaceX Crew Dragon Freedom spacecraft, carrying NASA astronauts Jessica Meir and Jack Hathaway, ESA astronaut Sophie Adenot, and Roscosmos cosmonaut Andrey Fedyaev, successfully splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of California on October 8, 2026.
stories.significance: This event marks the successful completion of the Crew-12 mission, returning the astronauts safely to Earth after nearly eight months aboard the International Space Station, demonstrating continued international collaboration and operational capability in human spaceflight.

stories.title: NASA’s SPHEREx Telescope Sees Menagerie of Brown Dwarfs
stories.summary: NASA's SPHEREx telescope has detected chemically rich atmospheres on brown dwarfs, containing molecules like water, carbon dioxide, carbon monoxide, and methane.
stories.finding: NASA's SPHEREx telescope has detected chemically rich atmospheres on brown dwarfs, containing molecules like water, carbon dioxide, carbon monoxide, and methane.
stories.significance: These findings reveal that brown dwarfs, which blur the line between stars and exoplanets, have complex atmospheres similar to those of giant planets in our solar system, challenging existing models.
stories.caveat: The source indicates that current theoretical models struggle to match the observed data, particularly concerning cloudy transitions in brown dwarf atmospheres, suggesting a need for further investigation.

stories.title: NSF–UKRI metascience statement
stories.summary: The US National Science Foundation (NSF) and UK Research and Innovation (UKRI) will collaborate on metascience, applying scientific methods to study and improve how research is funded, practiced, and evaluated.
stories.finding: The US National Science Foundation (NSF) and UK Research and Innovation (UKRI) will collaborate on metascience, applying scientific methods to study and improve how research is funded, practiced, and evaluated.
stories.significance: This partnership aims to enhance the effectiveness and efficiency of scientific endeavors by treating the scientific enterprise itself as a subject of study and improvement.
stories.caveat: The article outlines intentions and future plans for collaboration, with specific joint work to be identified in the coming months.

stories.title: Solar Orbiter tracks origin of mysterious magnetic switchbacks
stories.summary: The Solar Orbiter spacecraft has traced the origin of a magnetic switchback in the solar wind back to the Sun's surface, identifying a specific mix of charged oxygen and carbon particles that formed in hot magnetic field loops at the Sun's surface. This suggests that both interchange reconnection and waves/turbulence are involved in switchback formation, operating at different stages.
stories.finding: The Solar Orbiter spacecraft has traced the origin of a magnetic switchback in the solar wind back to the Sun's surface, identifying a specific mix of charged oxygen and carbon particles that formed in hot magnetic field loops at the Sun's surface. This suggests that both interchange reconnection and waves/turbulence are involved in switchback formation, operating at different stages.
stories.significance: Understanding the formation and movement of magnetic switchbacks helps explain how the Sun heats its atmosphere and accelerates solar wind particles. This knowledge is crucial for predicting and preparing for extreme space weather events that can impact infrastructure and technology on Earth and in space.
stories.caveat: The source does not specify material limitations; independent verification is not established.

stories.title: As voters weigh incumbents, U-M research complicates case for congressional term limits
stories.summary: Experienced lawmakers' offices develop greater capacity to assist constituents with navigating federal agencies, a function that constitutes about half of their work.
stories.finding: Experienced lawmakers' offices develop greater capacity to assist constituents with navigating federal agencies, a function that constitutes about half of their work.
stories.significance: This finding challenges the common justification for term limits, which often assumes lawmakers become less responsive over time, and suggests that the "startup costs" of new offices may hinder constituent service and policy work.
stories.caveat: The source does not specify material limitations; independent verification is not established.
entities: Gerald R. Ford School of Public Policy

stories.title: Mars’s oddest cloud may be even odder than we thought
stories.summary: Scientists have modeled Mars's Arsia Mons Elongated Cloud (AMEC) and found that its formation likely involves homogeneous nucleation, a process where water vapor directly freezes into ice particles without needing atmospheric specks, a phenomenon previously considered theoretical and unobserved in planetary atmospheres.
stories.finding: Scientists have modeled Mars's Arsia Mons Elongated Cloud (AMEC) and found that its formation likely involves homogeneous nucleation, a process where water vapor directly freezes into ice particles without needing atmospheric specks, a phenomenon previously considered theoretical and unobserved in planetary atmospheres.
stories.significance: This finding suggests that Mars's atmosphere can reach extreme humidity levels, enabling rare physical processes to occur, and highlights the importance of considering unlikely atmospheric phenomena when exploring planets.
stories.caveat: While the modeling successfully reproduced the AMEC, some aspects do not exactly match observations, and the source does not specify material limitations; independent verification is not established.

stories.title: Polarized America obsesses over small voting problems—or sweeps issues under rug
stories.summary: Testing has revealed that some election systems, which are not supposed to be connected to the internet, have been compromised. The slow process of patching these systems is a significant concern, especially with the rapid advancement of AI's ability to discover vulnerabilities.
stories.finding: Testing has revealed that some election systems, which are not supposed to be connected to the internet, have been compromised. The slow process of patching these systems is a significant concern, especially with the rapid advancement of AI's ability to discover vulnerabilities.
stories.significance: Hand-marked paper ballots are identified as the most secure election technology currently available. The findings highlight the need for policy reform to ensure election technology vendors identify security problems more effectively and that states promptly apply available security patches.
stories.caveat: While vulnerabilities have been identified, there is no evidence that these flaws have been exploited to alter election outcomes. The article does not specify material limitations of the testing or independent verification status.
stories.localConnection: University of Michigan research in Ann Arbor.

stories.title: Podcast: Could holographic 3D printing be real?

stories.title: NASA’s Curiosity Rover Catches Stunning Martian Dawn
stories.summary: NASA's Curiosity rover captured a detailed panorama of wind-carved Martian cliffs known as yardangs, revealing striking blue hues in the early morning light.
stories.finding: NASA's Curiosity rover captured a detailed panorama of wind-carved Martian cliffs known as yardangs, revealing striking blue hues in the early morning light.
stories.significance: This image provides the most detailed view yet of these distant Martian features, which scientists are eager to study to understand their formation and the history of Mars.
stories.caveat: The exact cause of the yardang layer remains uncertain, with one hypothesis suggesting it may be ash from ancient volcanic eruptions. Further data collection is planned.

stories.title: Webb captures commotion from nebula’s stellar jets
stories.summary: The James Webb Space Telescope has revealed previously hidden stars in the NGC 7129 stellar nursery, using infrared light to penetrate dust clouds. It observed a central star, LkH(alpha) 234, and its surrounding outflows and younger stars, showing different stages of stellar evolution and their impact on the environment.

stories.significance: This observation provides insight into how stars form and evolve, and how they shape their surrounding molecular clouds, potentially influencing future star formation and the eventual erosion of these clouds over millions of years.

stories.title: Abortion bans make healthcare more expensive
stories.summary: State abortion bans implemented after the Supreme Court's Dobbs decision are associated with increased out-of-pocket health insurance premium costs for women, with a more pronounced impact on Black and Hispanic women.

stories.title: Flu clues: Digging into 15 years of household data
stories.summary: The University of Michigan received a $14.2 million grant from the National Institutes of Health to establish the Michigan Center for Research on Influenza Transmission (MiCRIT). This center will analyze 15 years of household flu transmission data and collect new data to better understand and prevent person-to-person flu spread.

stories.significance: Improved understanding of human flu transmission can lead to more effective prevention strategies, reducing the significant global burden of illness, death, and economic losses caused by influenza. This research aims to overcome limitations of animal and experimental models by focusing on real-world human transmission factors.

stories.title: Steering wheel communicates for better semi-autonomous driving performance
stories.summary: A specialized steering wheel that allows for negotiation between human drivers and an autonomous driving simulation improved driving performance and increased trust between the driver and autonomous vehicle features.
stories.finding: A specialized steering wheel that allows for negotiation between human drivers and an autonomous driving simulation improved driving performance and increased trust between the driver and autonomous vehicle features.
stories.significance: This two-way communication system, unlike current one-way warning systems, could enhance the effectiveness and acceptance of semi-autonomous vehicles by fostering better teamwork and reducing driver stress and confusion.
stories.caveat: While the negotiation system improved trust recovery, some drivers became overly trusting after successful negotiations, indicating a need for further study on trust dynamics with such a system.
stories.localConnection: University of Michigan research in Ann Arbor.

stories.title: Science begins for Smile
stories.summary: The European-Chinese Smile mission has been declared ready to begin science operations, following a commissioning period after its launch on May 19 and reaching its target orbit on June 20.
stories.finding: The European-Chinese Smile mission has been declared ready to begin science operations, following a commissioning period after its launch on May 19 and reaching its target orbit on June 20.
stories.significance: The mission will study how Earth responds to solar wind, aiming to improve understanding of solar storms, geomagnetic storms, and space weather.
stories.caveat: While the soft X-ray imager (SXI) is working well, it is currently detecting too much unwanted stray light when pointed at Earth. Adjustments are being made, and the unwanted light is expected to naturally decrease by mid-October.

stories.title: Happy New Year on Mars
stories.summary: The 39th Martian year will commence on September 30, 2026, at 10:16 CEST/08:16 UTC, marking the Red Planet's new orbit around the Sun. A Martian year is approximately 687 Earth days, or 668 sols, nearly twice the length of an Earth year. Martian seasons vary in length due to Mars' elliptical orbit, and the second half of the Martian year is often characterized by intense dust storms.

stories.title: Galaxies in a cosmic house of mirrors
stories.summary: The James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) has observed gravitationally lensed galaxies, including a galaxy group 2 billion years after the Big Bang undergoing a merger with an enormous burst of star formation, and a single galaxy just 800 million years after the Big Bang. It also identified individual bright 'knots' within these lensed areas, corresponding to regions as small as 5 light-years across, magnified by a factor of more than 300.
stories.finding: The James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) has observed gravitationally lensed galaxies, including a galaxy group 2 billion years after the Big Bang undergoing a merger with an enormous burst of star formation, and a single galaxy just 800 million years after the Big Bang. stories.significance: Gravitational lensing, as observed by JWST, allows astronomers to study very distant and faint objects in the early Universe that would otherwise be undetectable. This capability provides unprecedented detail into early galaxy formation, mergers, and star formation processes, offering insights into the Universe's evolution.
stories.caveat: The source does not specify material limitations; independent verification is not established.

stories.title: Successful Earth flyby improves Juice’s course to Jupiter
stories.summary: The Jupiter Icy Moons Explorer (Juice) successfully completed an Earth flyby on September 28, 2026, using Earth's gravity to alter its trajectory towards Jupiter and increase its velocity by 3.5 km/s, while also testing its science instruments.
stories.finding: The Jupiter Icy Moons Explorer (Juice) successfully completed an Earth flyby on September 28, 2026, using Earth's gravity to alter its trajectory towards Jupiter and increase its velocity by 3.5 km/s, while also testing its science instruments.

stories.title: NASA Selects Far-Infrared Telescope as First in New Mission Class
stories.summary: NASA has selected the PRIMA (PRobe far-Infrared Mission for Astrophysics) space telescope to advance to the next phase of development, marking it as the first mission in a new class of NASA astrophysics missions called Probe Explorers.
stories.finding: NASA has selected the PRIMA (PRobe far-Infrared Mission for Astrophysics) space telescope to advance to the next phase of development, marking it as the first mission in a new class of NASA astrophysics missions called Probe Explorers.
stories.significance: PRIMA will serve as a new window into the deep universe, studying the formation of planets, stars, black holes, and the origin of water on Earth by conducting deep, sensitive surveys in far-infrared light. This will help bridge the gap between existing infrared and radio observatories, providing a more comprehensive look at the cosmos.
stories.caveat: The PRIMA mission is subject to a confirmation review based on technical, programmatic, and cost performance before it can begin implementation. Its project cost is capped at $1.2 billion, excluding launch and other non-project costs.

stories.title: Podcast: Can prosthetic limbs feel touch? (haptic feedback)

stories.title: A galaxy spinning out of sync

stories.title: NSF invests in translating low-dimensional semiconductor technologies to establish U.S. leadership in microelectronics

stories.title: NSF announces 3 additional topics as part of the NSF X-Labs initiative to pursue generational breakthrough science and technology efforts

stories.title: NASA Watches Earth’s Weight, Finds Center of Mass

stories.title: USGS detects zebra mussel environmental DNA in Utah’s Colorado River for the first time
stories.summary: Autonomous eDNA samplers deployed near the Colorado River by Moab found zebra mussel genetic material in June and July, the first such detection in Utah. stories.caveat: The detection establishes zebra mussel DNA, not a confirmed living population; follow-up sampling is needed to determine whether mussels themselves are present.

stories.title: How 2 US, European Satellites Are Studying Hurricanes During El Niño
stories.summary: The Sentinel-6B satellite, launched in November, is now flying behind its predecessor, Sentinel-6 Michael Freilich, to provide precise sea level height measurements that will improve hurricane forecasts.

stories.title: Chandra finds a new class of ultraviolet-bright, hypersoft X-ray sources
stories.summary: Researchers mining Chandra observations of six galaxies identified 84 ‘hypersoft X-ray sources’ that emit unusually low-energy X-rays alongside intense ultraviolet radiation. Their spectral signature is unlike any known class and points to compact objects—possibly white dwarfs, neutron stars, or black holes—accreting from companions; the population could help account for missing Type Ia supernova progenitors and a poorly explained source of interstellar-gas ionization.
stories.caveat: The study has not yet identified what physical systems produce the hypersoft X-ray sources; their link to Type Ia progenitors and interstellar-gas ionization remains a proposed explanation.

stories.title: Hubble and Webb reveal tiny outer-solar-system objects still preserve their origins
stories.summary: Joint Hubble and Webb observations discovered 27 exceptionally faint trans-Neptunian objects and measured their colors, sizes, and orbits in the deepest survey of its kind. The smallest observed body is about 5 kilometres across; surprisingly, these tiny objects retain the same color signatures as larger relatives and are less numerous than some planet-formation models predict, constraining how primordial planetesimals formed beyond Neptune.
stories.caveat: The reason the smallest bodies retain their original-looking surfaces remains unresolved; the teams are still assessing whether collisions are rarer than expected or whether the objects preserve primordial compositions.

stories.title: NASA’s X-59 completes 25 flights with flight behavior matching its models
stories.summary: NASA’s quiet-supersonic X-59 research aircraft has completed 25 test flights, including a 72-minute flight to Mach 1.2 and 49,000 feet. NASA reports that its handling, stability margin, and flight loads have closely matched the preflight digital-twin predictions, without unexpected aerodynamic instability or excessive vibration—clearing the way for acoustic-validation flights that will directly measure its low-boom sonic thumps.
stories.caveat: The key low-boom claim is not yet validated: NASA’s dedicated acoustic measurement campaign is the next phase.

stories.title: BepiColombo successfully sheds its transfer stage on approach to Mercury
stories.summary: After almost eight years and billions of kilometres in flight, ESA and JAXA’s BepiColombo mission successfully separated its Mercury Transfer Module more than 200 million kilometres from Earth. The Mercury Planetary Orbiter and Magnetospheric Orbiter are now operating as a composite spacecraft on the next leg toward Mercury orbit insertion in November, a key milestone toward the first two-spacecraft scientific mission at the planet.
stories.caveat: The two orbiters have not yet entered Mercury orbit; ESA schedules orbital insertion for November 2026 and science operations for April 2027.

stories.title: A multi-sensor rocket finds unexpected structure in radio-disrupting ionospheric clouds
stories.summary: New peer-reviewed results from NASA’s SpEED Demon sounding rocket provide the first simultaneous multi-point measurements inside a sporadic-E layer, a metal-ion cloud that can disrupt long-distance radio and GPS signals. Five detectors showed the layer was uneven and structured rather than a simple sheet, including a split into two peaks during descent—evidence that atmospheric turbulence shapes the plasma.
stories.caveat: The proposed Kelvin–Helmholtz turbulence explanation is plausible but unconfirmed because the flight did not directly measure local winds and electric fields.

stories.title: Hubble finds a giant, evolving decagon around Saturn’s south pole
stories.summary: NASA’s Hubble observations have revealed a 10-sided atmospheric wave embedded in Saturn’s south-polar jet stream—the first large regular-sided jet pattern seen in the planet’s southern hemisphere. The structure reaches through multiple atmospheric layers and had faint precursors in data from 2023, giving researchers a chance to watch a giant-planet circulation pattern develop.
stories.caveat: Scientists do not yet know whether the new decagon will become a long-lived stable feature like Saturn’s northern hexagon or continue evolving.

stories.title: Satellite record reveals a rapid post-2014 intensification of the Gulf Stream
stories.summary: A NOAA and University of Miami study of 31 years of satellite-altimeter observations found that the Gulf Stream downstream of the Florida Straits weakened until 2014, then shifted northward, stabilized, and rapidly strengthened through 2023. The result ties the change to wind-driven strengthening of the subtropical gyre and matters for North Atlantic heat transport, weather, sea level, and marine ecosystems.

source.name: NOAA Atlantic Oceanographic and Meteorological Laboratory

stories.caveat: The observed downstream Gulf Stream change should not be read as a direct measure of the broader Atlantic Meridional Overturning Circulation (AMOC), which responds to different forcings.

stories.title: ESA records a precision-targeted satellite reentry for debris science
stories.summary: ESA deliberately guided the Cluster satellite Samba to a remote South Pacific reentry and flew an instrumented aircraft from Tonga to observe it. The satellite reentered at 21:39:38 UTC on August 31, with the final prediction accurate to the second; 29 of 30 airborne instruments recorded its breakup, yielding rare measurements of how a spacecraft heats, fragments, and sheds materials.
stories.caveat: ESA says the images and instrument data are still being processed, so detailed material-by-material results are not yet available.

stories.title: Podcast: Lasers and materials of the future
stories.summary: Chunlei Guo, an NSF-supported researcher, is working on designing materials with highly functionalized purposes using femtosecond lasers.
stories.finding: Chunlei Guo, an NSF-supported researcher, is working on designing materials with highly functionalized purposes using femtosecond lasers.
stories.significance: This research could lead to advances in materials science, similar to past innovations like nylon stockings and artificial joints, by enabling the creation of materials with specific and advanced functionalities.
stories.caveat: The source does not specify material limitations; independent verification is not established.

stories.title: NOAA’s long-range robots extend a seafloor survey where ships cannot go
stories.summary: NOAA Fisheries sent two long-range autonomous underwater vehicles along more than 200 nautical miles of Mid-Atlantic seafloor track lines, collecting over 68,000 images for the Atlantic sea-scallop assessment. Their camera, environmental, and navigation systems can sample inside and around offshore infrastructure where traditional survey vessels cannot safely operate; NOAA says comparable robot data have already passed technical review and entered annual abundance estimates.

stories.title: NASA’s Dark Universe-Seeking Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope Launches
stories.summary: NASA's Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope has successfully launched and is beginning its journey to its final orbit, where it will study dark matter, dark energy, and exoplanets.
stories.finding: NASA's Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope has successfully launched and is beginning its journey to its final orbit, where it will study dark matter, dark energy, and exoplanets.
stories.significance: The telescope's large field of view and infrared vision will enable it to survey vast areas of the sky, potentially answering profound questions about cosmic history and the search for life beyond our solar system.
stories.caveat: The article focuses on the launch and initial deployment of the telescope's components, with scientific findings expected in the future.

stories.title: NASA’s Roman telescope launches toward its dark-universe survey
stories.summary: NASA’s Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope launched aboard a Falcon Heavy and separated from the rocket’s second stage, beginning its roughly three-month journey to the Sun–Earth L2 point. After commissioning, Roman will conduct wide, deep visible-to-near-infrared surveys to probe dark energy and dark matter and build a census of exoplanets.

stories.title: NASA’s Swift observatory resumes X-ray and ultraviolet science
stories.summary: NASA has restarted Swift’s X-ray and ultraviolet/optical instruments after months in low-drag mode intended to preserve the observatory for an attempted orbital boost. The boost spacecraft will no longer capture Swift, but the 21-year-old mission can again rapidly observe transient cosmic events while NASA estimates it has roughly one to two months above the altitude where operations become difficult.
stories.caveat: Swift’s third instrument, the Burst Alert Telescope, remains offline as the team works to return it to data collection.

stories.title: Europe launches a high-frequency weather imager for severe-storm nowcasting
stories.summary: ESA launched the MTG-I2 weather satellite aboard Ariane 6, completing the first operational trio of Meteosat Third Generation satellites. Once commissioned, its Flexible Combined Imager and Lightning Imager will provide high-resolution views of developing weather across Europe and northern Africa every 2.5 minutes, strengthening severe-weather, wildfire, pollution, and climate monitoring.

stories.title: NASA begins its most flight-relevant lunar landing plume tests
stories.summary: NASA has begun firing a simulated lander plume into lunar-regolith simulant inside a 60-foot vacuum sphere at Langley. Cameras and other instruments are measuring crater formation, ejecta geometry, and particle speeds to validate models for how rocket exhaust could endanger landers, surface equipment, and crews on the Moon—and eventually help prepare for Mars landings.

stories.title: New Next-Gen Dish Adds Muscle to NASA’s Deep Space Network
stories.summary: NASA's Deep Space Network facility in California has added a new 34-meter-wide radio frequency antenna, Deep Space Station 23 (DSS-23), which began operations on August 3, tracking missions such as NASA's Chandra X-ray Observatory, Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter, Psyche, Juno, and Voyager 1.
stories.finding: NASA's Deep Space Network facility in California has added a new 34-meter-wide radio frequency antenna, Deep Space Station 23 (DSS-23), which began operations on August 3, tracking missions such as NASA's Chandra X-ray Observatory, Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter, Psyche, Juno, and Voyager 1.
stories.significance: This new antenna strengthens NASA's deep space communications infrastructure, enabling support for more missions exploring the solar system and interstellar space, and enhancing the agency's capabilities for future space exploration endeavors.
stories.caveat: The source does not specify material limitations; independent verification is not established.

stories.title: NASA's Roman telescope clears its flight-readiness review
stories.summary: NASA and SpaceX certified the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope to proceed into final launch preparations, targeting no earlier than 7:26 a.m. EDT on August 30 aboard Falcon Heavy. Roman's wide-field surveys are designed to study dark energy, dark matter, exoplanets, and the universe's evolution.

stories.title: NASA's Starling satellites demonstrate GPS-free autonomous navigation
stories.summary: The FALCON experiment used onboard cameras and a catalog of space objects to determine Starling's orbit without GPS or ground navigation. Over three days it also improved orbit estimates for more than 200 tracked objects, a step toward autonomous lunar satellite swarms and better collision avoidance.

stories.title: Hubble identifies a major merger from the Milky Way’s infancy
stories.summary: Hubble measurements of 39 inner-Milky-Way globular clusters, combined with Gaia data, isolate a third cluster population that points to an ancient collision with a dwarf galaxy dubbed LKH. The result pushes definitive evidence of the Galaxy’s assembly history about 1.8 billion years farther back, to roughly 11.8 billion years ago.
